# 2013 Green Bay Packers–Dallas Cowboys Game

The December 15, 2013, National Football League (NFL) regular-season matchup between the Green Bay Packers and the Dallas Cowboys stands as one of the most dramatic and improbable games in modern league history , . Played at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, the contest saw the Packers overcome a staggering 23-point deficit at halftime to defeat the Cowboys 37–36 , , . This result was not only a testament to the Packers' resilience but also marked a historic moment for both franchises. For the Packers, it represented the largest comeback in their storied franchise history, tying a previous record set in a 1982 game against the Los Angeles Rams , . Conversely, for the Cowboys, the loss was a catastrophic implosion, as it became the first instance in their entire 57-year history that they had ever lost a game after holding a lead of 20 points or more at the half; their record in such situations prior to this game was a perfect 46–0 . The game was broadcast nationally on Fox, with Joe Buck and Troy Aikman providing commentary for the television audience . The attendance for the Week 15 clash was 91,054 spectators, who witnessed an unforgettable reversal of fortune , . The victory kept the Packers' slim playoff hopes alive during a critical stretch of the NFC North race, while the devastating loss dealt a severe blow to the Cowboys' aspirations in the NFC East , .

## Background and Context

The Week 15 encounter between the Green Bay Packers and the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, December 15, 2013, held significant weight for both teams as they navigated a competitive and crucial phase of the 2013 NFL season . The Packers entered the game with a challenging 6–6–1 record, placing them in a precarious position within the tightly contested NFC North division . Their slim playoff hopes were on the line, and a victory against a fellow playoff contender like the Cowboys was essential to keep their postseason aspirations from slipping away , . The Packers' path to contention would remain difficult, with upcoming games against the Pittsburgh Steelers and on the road against the Chicago Bears . In contrast, the Dallas Cowboys came into the matchup with a respectable 7–6 record, positioning themselves as a formidable force in the NFC East . As defending division champions, the Cowboys were actively trying to solidify their hold on the top spot in the division and secure home-field advantage throughout the playoffs . The winner of this game stood to gain a substantial advantage in the standings, making the matchup a de facto "game of survival" for both franchises.

The stage for this pivotal contest was set at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, a venue known for its large crowds and electric atmosphere , . The game was scheduled for a 3:25 p.m. CST kickoff and was televised nationally on the Fox network, with the broadcasting team of Joe Buck, Troy Aikman, and Pam Oliver calling the action for millions of viewers across the country . The official assigned to oversee the game was referee Walt Coleman . Prior to the game, the Cowboys were favored to win by four points, reflecting the perception that their strong start to the season would give them an edge over the struggling Packers . However, the pre-game narrative failed to account for the seismic shift in momentum that would define the afternoon. The Cowboys' offensive prowess, particularly in the first half, was expected to pose a significant threat to the Packers' defense, while the Packers' offense was seen as vulnerable without its star quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, who was sidelined with an injury , . The absence of Rodgers meant that the Packers' starting quarterback duties fell to Matt Flynn, a move that would ultimately become central to the story of this historic comeback , . The stage was therefore set for a clash between two determined teams, where the outcome would have profound implications for their respective seasons. The game was not just a regular-season affair; it was a high-stakes battle that would test the mettle of both organizations and deliver one of the most memorable finishes of the year .

## First Half Dominance by the Cowboys

The first half of the December 15, 2013, game between the Green Bay Packers and the Dallas Cowboys was a masterclass in offensive execution by the host team, resulting in one of the most dominant performances in franchise history and a crushing 26–3 lead at the end of the second quarter , , . From the opening drive, the Cowboys' offense, led by quarterback Tony Romo, established a punishing rhythm that overwhelmed the Packers' defense . Dallas began the scoring process early in the first quarter, taking a 3–0 lead when kicker Dan Bailey connected on a 47-yard field goal at the 10:56 mark , . The Packers responded quickly with a field goal of their own, Mason Crosby booting a 57-yarder to tie the score at 3–3 with 7:40 remaining in the quarter , . However, the tide turned decisively in favor of the Cowboys, who scored 23 unanswered points to seize control of the game. Dallas extended their lead with another Bailey field goal, this one from 23 yards out, followed by a spectacular 25-yard touchdown reception by tight end Jason Witten from Tony Romo, giving the Cowboys a 13–3 advantage at the end of the first quarter , . The Cowboys' dominance continued unabated into the second quarter. Bailey added three more field goals, from distances of 43, 50, and another 50 yards, showcasing his leg strength and contributing significantly to the burgeoning lead , . The final score of the first half belonged entirely to the Cowboys, culminating in a one-yard touchdown run by running back DeMarco Murray, which capped off a seven-play, 75-yard drive and sent the Dallas Cowboys to the locker room with a commanding 26–3 lead , .

The statistical disparity in the first half was stark, underscoring the extent of the Cowboys' offensive explosion. Dallas amassed a franchise-record 332 total yards in the first two quarters alone, while Green Bay managed only 33 yards . The Cowboys' average drive started from their own 29.7-yard line and lasted a mere 2:32, highlighting their efficiency and ability to quickly move the ball down the field . By halftime, the Cowboys had already recorded 27 first downs and forced the Packers into multiple three-and-outs . Their success was built on a potent combination of a dynamic passing attack and a powerful ground game. Tony Romo was surgical through the air, completing passes with precision, while DeMarco Murray consistently broke tackles and found daylight, finishing the first half with 93 rushing yards on just 11 carries, averaging an impressive 7.4 yards per attempt . The Packers' defense, which had been a strength for much of the season, appeared completely unprepared for the onslaught. They were unable to contain either the run or the pass, allowing the Cowboys to dictate the pace and tempo of the game from the outset . The sheer scale of the deficit facing the Packers at halftime—23 points—was unprecedented and seemed insurmountable, casting a long shadow over the remainder of the contest , . Head coach Mike McCarthy and the Packers' coaching staff had little time to regroup and devise a strategy to counter the overwhelming force they faced, as the second half loomed with a mountain to climb .

## The Historic Second-Half Comeback

The second half of the 2013 Green Bay Packers–Dallas Cowboys game was a breathtaking display of football, defined by an unprecedented turnaround that saw the Packers erase a 23-point deficit to win 37–36 , . After entering the locker room trailing 26–3, the Packers emerged with a newfound resolve and a new leader under center, Matt Flynn, who stepped in for the injured Aaron Rodgers , . The catalyst for the comeback was a 60-yard run by running back Eddie Lacy, which sparked the Packers' offensive surge and ignited the dormant Lambeau Field faithful watching on television . With renewed energy, the Packers' offense took the field and began methodically chipping away at the Dallas lead. The defining characteristic of the second-half rally was the Packers' ability to score on five consecutive possessions, a sequence that transformed the game's momentum and shattered the Cowboys' aura of invincibility , . The comeback was not a single play but a sustained period of dominance that showcased the resilience and talent of the Packers' roster. Each touchdown drive was crucial, slowly but surely dismantling the Cowboys' defense and erasing the memory of the disastrous first half.

The scoring summary of the second half perfectly illustrates the magnitude of the comeback. Green Bay opened the third quarter with a touchdown drive of their own, beginning with a 13-yard touchdown pass from Matt Flynn to Jordy Nelson, cutting the Dallas lead to 26–10 , . Although the Cowboys added a field goal from 50 yards out to extend their lead to 29–10, the Packers answered immediately with another touchdown, this time a 3-yard pass from Flynn to Andrew Quarless, bringing the score to 29–17 , . The Cowboys briefly regained some composure with a 5-yard touchdown catch by Dez Bryant, putting them up 36–17 late in the fourth quarter, but it was too little, too late , . The Packers then unleashed a furious final push. James Starks caught an 11-yard touchdown pass from Flynn, followed by a 3-yard touchdown reception from James Jones, tying the game at 36–36 with minutes remaining , . The decisive play came with 1:31 left on the clock, when Eddie Lacy powered in from one yard out for a touchdown, giving the Packers their first lead of the second half , . Despite a failed two-point conversion attempt, the Packers retained a one-point lead , . The Cowboys got one last chance, but a desperate heave from Tony Romo was intercepted by Tramon Williams, sealing the incredible victory for Green Bay , . One source noted that this interception was initially ruled an incomplete pass but was overturned on video review, adding a layer of officiating drama to the final moments of the game . This remarkable comeback, where the Packers scored 34 unanswered points, remains a cornerstone of Packers history and a cautionary tale for all sports teams about never counting anyone out until the final whistle , .

## Individual Performances and Key Plays

The outcome of the December 15, 2013, game was dictated by the extraordinary performances of several key players whose actions on the field directly influenced the dramatic turn of events. For the Green Bay Packers, the entire team contributed to the historic comeback, but the efforts of quarterback Matt Flynn and running back Eddie Lacy were paramount. Starting in place of the injured Aaron Rodgers, Matt Flynn engineered one of the most efficient second-half passing attacks in recent NFL history , . On 26-of-39 passing, Flynn threw for an astonishing 299 yards and four touchdowns, orchestrating five consecutive touchdown drives that fueled the Packers' rally , . His touchdown passes were spread across the offense, finding five different receivers: Jordy Nelson (twice), Andrew Quarless, James Starks, and James Jones, demonstrating a balanced and effective attack , . On the ground, Eddie Lacy was the engine of the Packers' offense, rushing for 141 yards on 21-22 carries and scoring a crucial one-yard touchdown with 1:31 remaining to put the Packers ahead for good , , . His performance was instrumental in keeping the Packers' offense moving and helped him reach 1,000 yards for the season . Defensively, the victory was sealed by cornerback Tramon Williams, who intercepted a desperation pass from Tony Romo with less than two minutes left, securing the win and cementing his place in Packers lore , .

For the Dallas Cowboys, the game was a tale of two halves, with their initial dominance collapsing in the face of a ferocious second-half assault. Quarterback Tony Romo was brilliant in the first half, throwing for 358 yards and two touchdowns, but his performance in the fourth quarter was the primary cause of the devastating loss , , . He threw for a total of 358 yards and two touchdowns in the game, but two critical interceptions thrown in the final minutes directly enabled the Packers' comeback , , . These turnovers occurred on the Cowboys' final two drives, nullifying a stated plan to run the ball and force Green Bay into timeouts, thereby dooming their chances of closing out the game . Wide receiver Dez Bryant provided a bright spot for Dallas, recording 11 receptions for 153 yards and a 5-yard touchdown catch late in the fourth quarter that gave the Cowboys a brief lead , , . Running back DeMarco Murray was also a key contributor in the first half, rushing for 134 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries, but received only seven attempts in the second half despite the large lead , . Kicker Dan Bailey was reliable, kicking five field goals in the game, including two from 50 yards out, but his success could not compensate for the offensive breakdowns that ultimately cost the Cowboys the game , . The contrast between these individual performances perfectly encapsulates the game's narrative: the Packers' collective heroics versus the Cowboys' singular failure to execute when it mattered most.

## Statistical Analysis and Team Comparison

A detailed comparison of the statistical outputs for the Green Bay Packers and Dallas Cowboys reveals the profound dichotomy between their performances in the first and second halves of the December 15, 2013, game. While the Cowboys dominated statistically in the first half, the Packers matched and surpassed them in nearly every major category in the second half, leading to their historic comeback victory. The final box score shows the Packers finishing with 433 total yards (283 passing, 150 rushing) and 26 first downs, compared to the Cowboys' 466 total yards (332 passing, 134 rushing) and 27 first downs , . At first glance, the teams appear similar, but a deeper look at their production by quarter tells a different story. In the first half, Dallas amassed 332 of their 466 total yards, while Green Bay managed only 33 yards . In the second half, the Packers produced 400 of their 433 total yards, while the Cowboys managed just 134 . This stark contrast highlights how the Packers' offensive resurgence was the sole reason they were able to overcome the massive deficit.

The Cowboys committed two costly interceptions in the fourth quarter, while the Packers' only turnover was an interception thrown by Matt Flynn , , . This one-turnover differential proved fatal for Dallas, as it allowed the Packers to maintain possession and sustain their offensive drives deep into the fourth quarter. The discrepancy in penalty yards was also significant, with Dallas committing 79 penalties for 80 yards compared to Green Bay's 27 penalty yards , . While the number of penalties was higher for Dallas, the yardage difference suggests that Green Bay's infractions were more costly, potentially costing them crucial yardage on key downs. In terms of special teams, Mason Crosby's 57-yard field goal for the Packers was a highlight, while Dan Bailey successfully converted four field goals, including two from 50 yards out , . The game serves as a clear example of how momentum, execution, and minimizing mistakes can dramatically alter the statistical landscape and determine the victor.

## Aftermath and Legacy

The aftermath of the 37–36 loss for the Dallas Cowboys was one of profound disappointment and disbelief, with team leadership offering candid assessments of the team's catastrophic second-half performance. Owner Jerry Jones described the defeat as "one of the hardest losses that I’ve experienced," expressing his anguish over squandering a 23-point lead and witnessing a dominant first-half showing evaporate . Head coach Jason Garrett provided a simple yet damning explanation, stating, "We played very well in the first half... and then we didn’t play well in the second half. It’s just as simple as that" . Cornerback Brandon Carr was even more direct, labeling the team's collapse a "complete debacle" . The loss dropped the Cowboys to a 7–7 record, leaving them one game behind the Philadelphia Eagles in the NFC East with two games remaining on the schedule , . Despite the poor result, owner Jones publicly reaffirmed his support for head coach Jason Garrett, stating unequivocally that he would remain in his position regardless of future outcomes . This immediate post-game fallout underscored the shock value of the loss and the difficulty of absorbing such a dramatic reversal of fortune. The game served as a painful reminder of the fragility of leads in professional football and the importance of sustained effort throughout all four quarters.

For the Green Bay Packers, the victory was a lifeline that kept their 2013 season alive . The team improved to a 7–7–1 record, preserving their slim playoff hopes during a critical stretch of the NFC North race , . The win was particularly sweet as it came against a division rival and featured a historic comeback that would be remembered for years to come. The game solidified the legacy of Matt Flynn, who delivered a career-defining performance in relief of Aaron Rodgers, and elevated Eddie Lacy to stardom with his explosive rushing day , . The victory provided a crucial morale boost for a team fighting to stay relevant in a tough conference. The game itself has since been immortalized in Packers history as one of their greatest comebacks, often cited in discussions of the franchise's most memorable victories , . It stands as a testament to the unpredictability of the NFL and the power of perseverance. The intense media coverage and widespread discussion surrounding the game ensured its lasting legacy, making it a reference point for debates on the greatest comebacks and collapses in sports history. The image of Tramon Williams intercepting Tony Romo to seal the win is etched in the memories of fans on both sides, symbolizing the dramatic pendulum swing that characterized this unforgettable contest.

The game itself has since been immortalized in Packers history as one of their greatest comebacks, often cited in discussions of the franchise's most memorable victories.
It stands as a testament to the unpredictability of the NFL and the power of perseverance.

The intense media coverage and widespread discussion surrounding the game ensured its lasting legacy, making it a reference point for debates on the greatest comebacks and collapses in sports history.

The image of Tramon Williams intercepting Tony Romo to seal the win is etched in the memories of fans on both sides, symbolizing the dramatic pendulum swing that characterized this unforgettable contest.

The [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") played an [American football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") game against the [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys") in Week 15 of the [2013 National Football League (NFL) season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NFL_season "2013 NFL season") on December 15, 2013, at [AT&T Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AT%26T_Stadium "AT&T Stadium") in [Arlington, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington,_Texas "Arlington, Texas"), United States. Both teams entered Week 15 with middling records, with the Packers sitting at 6–6–1 and the Cowboys at 7–6. The Packers started the season strong, yet a broken collarbone by quarterback [Aaron Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers") in Week 8 saw the Packers lose or tie five straight games under three different back-up quarterbacks. Both teams were coming off a loss in Week 14, although each of their playoff hopes were still alive and both still had a chance to win their respective divisions. The Cowboys started the game strong, taking a 26–3 lead going into halftime, with kicker [Dan Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Bailey_/(American_football/) "Dan Bailey (American football)") converting four field goals. [Matt Flynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Flynn_/(American_football/) "Matt Flynn (American football)"), who was playing in place of the injured Rodgers, helped the Packers storm back in the second half. He led the Packers to five touchdown drives, including four touchdown passes. The Packers defense was able to hold the Cowboys to just 10 points in the second half, with [Tramon Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tramon_Williams "Tramon Williams") sealing the victory with an interception of quarterback [Tony Romo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Romo "Tony Romo") with less than two minutes left in the game. The victory matched the Packers team record for the largest comeback at 23 points and helped them maintain the possibility of winning the [NFC North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_North "NFC North") and making the playoffs. Both teams entered the final week of the season with a chance to win their division; the Packers won, while the Cowboys lost. The Packers would make the playoffs yet lose in the first round to the [San Francisco 49ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers"). The [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") began the season as the defending [NFC North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_North "NFC North") champions, having won the division the previous two seasons.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-1) They began their season with a record of 5–2, although one of their losses came after surrendering a 16-point second half lead to the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals").[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-2013PACK-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-3) Their eighth game of the year was on _[Monday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monday_Night_Football "Monday Night Football")_ against the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears"). In the first quarter, [Aaron Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers") was injured, missing the rest of the game with what was later diagnosed as a broken collarbone.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-4) Rodgers would go on to miss the next seven games, with [Seneca Wallace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seneca_Wallace "Seneca Wallace"), [Scott Tolzien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Tolzien "Scott Tolzien"), and [Matt Flynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Flynn_/(American_football/) "Matt Flynn (American football)") all starting games in his place. Wallace was injured in his first game and the Packers signed Flynn, who had played for the Packers previously, midway through the season.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-5) The Packers went 0–4–1 during a five-game stretch which included the Bears game to bring their record to 5–6–1.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-2013PACK-2) The Packers played the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons") in Week 14 and fell behind 21–10 in the first half. However, Flynn led a comeback to beat the Falcons 22–21, evening the Packers record at 6–6–1 and keeping them in the hunt for the NFC North.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-6) The [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys") began the 2013 season having gone 8–8 in back-to-back seasons, missing the playoffs both times.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-7) The season was back-and-forth, with the Cowboys never winning more than two games in a row nor losing more than two games in a row. They entered Week 15 with a record of 7–6 after a loss to the Bears in Week 14.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-2013COW-8) The Cowboys were scheduled to host the Packers in Week 15 at [AT&T Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AT%26T_Stadium "AT&T Stadium") on December 15, 2013.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-PREVIEW-9) Both teams were mathematically still in the hunt for their respective division titles and needed a victory to improve their chances of making the playoffs.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-PREVIEW-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBraun201414-10) The Cowboys were favored by four points.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-11) [![Image 4: View of AT&T Stadium with a lake and trees in the foreground.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Cowboys_Stadium%2C_a_domed_stadium_with_a_retractable_roof_in_Arlington%2C_Texas_LCCN2013650777.tif/lossy-page1-250px-Cowboys_Stadium%2C_a_domed_stadium_with_a_retractable_roof_in_Arlington%2C_Texas_LCCN2013650777.tif.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cowboys_Stadium,_a_domed_stadium_with_a_retractable_roof_in_Arlington,_Texas_LCCN2013650777.tif) [AT&T Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AT%26T_Stadium "AT&T Stadium"), shown here in 2012, was the site of the Week 15 match-up between the Packers and Cowboys. The Cowboys started the game with possession of the ball. A 27-yard pass from [Tony Romo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Romo "Tony Romo") to [Terrance Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrance_Williams "Terrance Williams") got the Cowboys in scoring position, but the Packers got a stop on third down and forced a 47-yard field goal attempt, which [Dan Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Bailey_/(American_football/) "Dan Bailey (American football)") converted. The Packers matched the Cowboys on the next drive, going 41 yards in 6 plays to set-up a 57-yard field goal attempt. Almost all of the yardage on the drive came from a 39-yard pass from [Matt Flynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Flynn_/(American_football/) "Matt Flynn (American football)") to [James Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Jones_/(wide_receiver/) "James Jones (wide receiver)"). [Mason Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") converted the field goal, tying the game at 3–3. On the subsequent drive, [DeMarco Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeMarco_Murray "DeMarco Murray") had a 41-yard rush that put the Cowboys in scoring position, but again the Packers stopped the Cowboys on third down, with Bailey converting a 23-yard field goal to give the Cowboys the lead again, 6–3. After the Packers went [three-and-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-and-out "Three-and-out") and punted, the Cowboys quickly drove 65 yards in 4 plays, capped off by a 25-yard touchdown from Romo to [Jason Witten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Witten "Jason Witten"). The Cowboys lead increased to 13–3. On the first play of the next drive, Flynn threw deep to Jones and the Cowboys were called for a 31-yard defensive pass interference penalty. However, after a sack and two incomplete passes, the Packers were forced to punt again. Each team then exchanged punts after short drives. The Cowboys got the ball back and drove 48 yards in 8 plays, but again were stopped and had to attempt a field goal. Bailey converted his third field goal of the half, this time from 43 yards, to increase the Cowboys lead to 16–3. On the next drive, Flynn threw an interception to [Sterling Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sterling_Moore "Sterling Moore"), who returned it 21 yards. The Packers did not allow the Cowboys to gain any yardage on their drive, but they were already in field goal range. Bailey made his fourth field goal of the half, this time from 50 yards, bringing the score to 19–3. The Packers were again forced to punt on their next drive. Romo completed three passes on the next drive for a combined 70 yards, with Murray scoring a touchdown on a one-yard rush. The Packers attempted to score on the next drive, but they ran out of a time after a 34-yard screen pass from Flynn to [Eddie Lacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Lacy "Eddie Lacy") ended the first half. The Cowboys led 26–3 at halftime.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-PLAYBYPLAY-12) The Packers had possession of the ball to begin the second half. On the first play of their drive, Lacy had a 60-yard rush; three plays later Flynn threw a touchdown pass to [Jordy Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordy_Nelson "Jordy Nelson"), cutting the Cowboys lead to 26–10. The Cowboys responded, with Bailey kicking his fifth field goal, from 50 yards, of the game after an 11-play, 48-yard drive. On the ensuing drive, the Packers again travelled the length of the field, going 80 yards in 12 plays, and scoring on a 3-yard touchdown pass from Flynn to [Andrew Quarless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Quarless "Andrew Quarless"). After the Cowboys' field goal and Packers' touchdown, the score was 29–17. The Packers forced a three-and-out on the Cowboys' next drive after sacking Romo on third down. [Micah Hyde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micah_Hyde_/(American_football/) "Micah Hyde (American football)") returned the Cowboys' punt from mid-field 26 yards. The Packers scored five plays later on an 11-yard touchdown pass from Flynn to [James Starks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Starks "James Starks"). The Cowboys lead was now only five points, 29–24. On the Cowboys next drive, Romo threw a pass that appeared to be intercepted by [Tramon Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tramon_Williams "Tramon Williams"), however after replay review, the pass was called incomplete. The Cowboys capitalized, going the length of the field to score a touchdown on a short pass from Romo to [Dez Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dez_Bryant "Dez Bryant"). The Packers responded, going 80 yards in 10 plays to score, with Flynn completing a 3-yard pass to Jones for a touchdown. The Cowboys lead was cut back to five points again, with the score at 36–31. The Cowboys converted a third down with 12 yards to go on the next drive, but on the fifth play Romo threw an interception to [Sam Shields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Shields "Sam Shields") at mid-field. The Packers drove to the Cowboys' one-yard line with less than two minutes left in the game. Lacy scored a touchdown on a one-yard rush, with the Packers failing on the two-point conversion. Down for the first time in the game, 37–36, the Cowboys began their next drive with a nine-yard completion from Romo to [Cole Beasley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Beasley "Cole Beasley"). Romo's next pass was ruled incomplete, yet after replay review, the call was changed to an interception by Williams. The Packers ran out the rest of the game clock to secure the comeback victory.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-PLAYBYPLAY-12) | Game information | | --- | |

Post-game analysis focused on the Packers’ comeback and the significant differences for each team between the first and second half.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-VANDERMAUSE-16)[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-FEELING-17)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-18) The Packers' offense was only able to score three points in the first half, even though the Cowboys came into the game with the worst ranked defense in the NFL.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-THICK1-19)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-THICK2-20) The Packers' defense was able to stop the Cowboys offense on four drives, forcing field goals instead of touchdowns.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-PFRBOX-14) Even so, the Cowboys offense was able to move the ball through the air and on the ground and took a commanding 26–3 lead into halftime.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-THICK1-19)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-THICK2-20) Coming into the second half, the Packers decided to run the ball, with Lacy breaking free for a 60-yard rush that multiple players noted sparked the Packers’ offense.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-RUSHING-21) The Packers scored their first touchdown three plays later, starting a streak of five straight touchdown drives.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-FEELING-17) Other key plays were highlighted, including interceptions in the fourth quarter by Shields and Williams that helped the Packers gain the lead for the first time and seal their victory.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-FEELING-17)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-VANDERMAUSE-16) Individual performances were highlighted, especially on offense. Romo threw for 358 yards and two touchdowns, while Flynn had 299 passing yards and four touchdowns. Each team had a rusher eclipse 100 yards, with Lacy gaining 141 yards and Murray having 134 yards; each scored a touchdown.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NUMBERS-22) Boykin and Quarless led the Packers in receptions and yards, although Nelson’s performance on third down was specifically noted.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NUMBERS-22)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NELSON-23) On the Cowboys’ side, Bryant had a successful performance, catching 11 passes for 153 yards and a touchdown.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NUMBERS-22) His touchdown catch was praised for its level of difficulty.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NFL-24) After the game, decisions by the Cowboys coaching staff and Romo were questioned.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NFL-24) The Cowboys were very successful rushing the ball in the first half, with Murray going for 93 yards. However, in the second half, even with a large lead, the Cowboys only gave the ball to Murray seven times. Ironically, it was the Packers who saw a lot of success in the second half rushing the ball.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-RUSHING-21) This was very apparent on each Cowboys’ drive that ended in an interception, with post-game commentators questioning why the Cowboys were not trying to run out the clock and instead were throwing the ball downfield.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-NFL-24)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-25) Cowboys head coach [Jason Garrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Garrett "Jason Garrett") noted after the game that in hindsight the team should have called more running plays.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-RUSHING-21) After their victory, the Packers record was 7–6–1 and they were still in the hunt for the NFC North title. With Rodgers close to returning, the Packers hosted the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") at [Lambeau Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambeau_Field "Lambeau Field") in Week 16. In that game the Packers gave up a late score after a fumble by Flynn, but then had a long kickoff return by Micah Hyde. After a couple plays, the Packers got to the one-yard line, but a penalty pushed them back five yards and gave them just enough time to run a play to try to score. Flynn threw incomplete and the Packers lost, leaving them with 7–7–1 record. The Bears lost in Week 16 as well, setting up a match-up in Week 17 for the NFC North title between the Packers and Bears, who were hosting. Rodgers returned from his injury for the Bears game and threw a late touchdown pass on fourth down to seal the victory and the NFC North title for the Packers.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers%E2%80%93Dallas_Cowboys_game#cite_note-BEARS-26) The game against the Bears was named one of the 50 greatest sports moments in Wisconsin history in 2020 by the _[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Journal_Sentinel "Milwaukee Journal 3.content:
In Week 15, most of the top playoff contenders played on the road.

The [New England Patriots](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/ne/new-england-patriots) lost at Miami, but the real stunner was the [New Orleans Saints](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/no/new-orleans-saints)' 27-16 loss in St. Louis. Saints coach Sean Payton described the loss as "pretty ugly." It was. But so was the [Dallas Cowboys](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/dal/dallas-cowboys)' 37-36 home loss to the Green Bay Packers in which [Tony Romo](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/5209/tony-romo) threw two key interceptions down the stretch.

The impact of those losses was huge. Dallas remains a game behind a [Philadelphia Eagles](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/phi/philadelphia-eagles) team that lost to Minnesota on the road. But the Saints were the biggest losers. It's now clear to Payton that they aren't the same team on the road.

"You know that's where it is right now," Payton said. "We looked flat coming out. We can't line up to kick a field goal. We can't stop the run. ... At some point, you can't keep watching."

The Saints travel to Carolina in Week 16. They are now in jeopardy of losing the NFC South and being just a wild-card team forced to play on the road to get to the Super Bowl. That's a road the Saints don't want to take.

Here's what we learned in Week 15:

**1\. Limited without Gronk:** As expected, the absence of tight end [Rob Gronkowski](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/13229/rob-gronkowski) loomed large for the Patriots in a 24-20 loss to the Miami Dolphins. [Tom Brady](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/2330/tom-brady) & Co. scored only one touchdown in four tries inside the Dolphins' red zone.

In the first quarter, Brady had a 16-play field-goal drive for 83 yards that stalled at the Dolphins' 4-yard line after two incompletions to two different wide receivers. In the fourth quarter, the Patriots had a 15-play, 81-yard field-goal drive that was stopped at the Dolphins' 5. After the Dolphins took the lead with 1:15 left in the game, you knew Brady would have enough time to get the ball into the Dolphins' red zone. But in five plays from inside the Dolphins' 20, he had four incompletions and a game-ending interception.

Gronkowski would normally turn those opportunities into touchdowns. Coming into the game, Brady completed 16 of 25 passes to Gronkowski for eight touchdowns in the red zone.

"We didn't do a good job in the red zone," Brady conceded. "We didn't do a good job of finishing off drives."

Without Gronkowski, the Patriots are settling in as a team that scores in the twenties instead of the thirties, and that could cost New England a top seed and maybe even a playoff bye. The Patriots will find it difficult to win games on the road in the playoffs scoring only around 20 points a game.

**2\. Speed bump in Minnesota:** On Jan. 18, the city of Minneapolis is taking the air out of the soon-to-be vacant Mall of America Dome. On Sunday, the Vikings took some of the air out of the Eagles' playoff run. An Eagle team that had been soaring looked disrupted in a 48-30 loss to the Vikings. Not only was the Eagles' defense shredded by Vikings backup QB [Matt Cassel](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/8644/matt-cassel), but Chip Kelly's offense was out of sync.

Eagles wide receiver [DeSean Jackson](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/11283/desean-jackson) got into a shouting match with teammates and coaches after a third-quarter pass to him was intercepted by the Vikings. Kelly called that decorum unacceptable and said he would talk to Jackson and his position coach. If Jackson's shouting was unacceptable, the loss was even worse. The Vikings were missing their top two running backs -- [Adrian Peterson](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/10452/adrian-peterson) and [Toby Gerhart](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/13211/toby-gerhart) -- and featured [Matt Asiata](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/14360/matt-asiata), who had only three carries in his NFL career before Sunday.

"We didn't execute on offense," Kelly said. "We didn't play well enough to win the game."

But listening to Kelly after the game made me feel as though the Eagles can still win the NFC East. His words had some meaning because he brought the team together after a bad start, allowing it to go on a five-game winning streak.

"We need to stick together," Kelly said. "It's what we did when we were 3-5. It's what we need to do now to finish this off the right way." It won't be easy. The Eagles, who lead the Cowboys by one game in the division, host the Chicago Bears on Sunday night and finish the season on the road against Dallas.

**3\. Cutler shakes off rust:** In the first half of the Bears' 38-31 victory at Cleveland, a lot of Chicago fans were likely thinking "I told you so," with regard to coach Marc Trestman's decision to go with [Jay Cutler](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/9597/jay-cutler) instead of the hot [Josh McCown](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/3609/josh-mccown) at quarterback. Cutler's fourth pass was intercepted by Browns safety [Tashaun Gipson](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/15235/tashaun-gipson). In the second quarter, Gipson turned a Cutler interception into a pick-six. It was Gipson who said earlier in the week that Cutler has a tendency to throw it up to defenders.

Cutler, however, took control of the game in the fourth quarter by completing five of seven passes for 71 yards and two touchdowns. He led three touchdown drives to clinch a much-needed win.

"I started rusty," Cutler said. "The guys rallied around me. It was a fun, fun game."

Everyone, including Cutler, knows McCown put up strong numbers during Cutler's absence, but it also has to be noted that those games were against beatable defenses. Two of McCown's 350-plus-yard games were against St. Louis and Minnesota, and the Bears lost those games. The postgame interviews of [Brandon Marshall](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/9705/brandon-marshall) and Cutler confirmed why most the team and coaching staff were on the same page going to Cutler. Marshall admitted he made a mistake on the first interception by running the route. The pick-six? Marshall said that was on Cutler. "He stunk on that one," Marshall said. He laughed and so did Cutler.

Marshall knows the ride with Cutler can be bumpy. He mentioned the debate of the 2010 NFC Championship Game in which Cutler couldn't finish because of knee injury. He knows Cutler will throw some picks. But Marshall and Cutler are friends and Cutler's other teammates respect him. Trestman was right in going to him, and now general manager Phil Emory has to be right after the season and give Cutler a contract extension.

**4\. Loss for the ages:** The Cowboys blew a 23-point lead and lost to Green Bay. Once again, it was Romo making the mistakes and the coaching staff not being able to close out a game.

After the game, Cowboys coach Jason Garrett said the plan was to run the ball and force the Packers to call timeouts. But Romo, who has the freedom to switch between running plays and passing plays, ran only one running play on Dallas' final two drives. Both possessions resulted in interceptions, helping Green Bay overcome a late, 12-point deficit.

It was the greatest choke job in Cowboys history. The Cowboys were 46-0 all time when they had at least a 20-point halftime lead. The NFC East was theirs to claim and once again Romo and the Cowboys are blowing it.

**5\. Heat's on Lions:** Trestman's decision to go with Cutler helped the Bears beat Cleveland. Sheer guts enabled the Packers to overcome a 23-point halftime lead to beat Dallas. If the Lions lose at home to Baltimore on Monday night, they might blow their chance to win the NFC North.

No doubt the Packers had the gutsiest performance Sunday. The Cowboys were shredding them. A sad [Aaron Rodgers](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/8439/aaron-rodgers) was on the sidelines in street close because Dr. Pat McKenzie didn't believe Rodgers' fractured left collarbone had healed. The Packers had backup [Matt Flynn](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/11443/matt-flynn) and what seemed like a remote chance to win.

"When you put yourself in a hole, you have to fight, scratch and claw," Packers coach Mike McCarthy said. "For us to get those turnovers was huge."

At 7-6-1, the Packers have a chance. If they get Rodgers back next week, they might win out and make the playoffs.

#### SHORT TAKES

The decision by Washington Redskins coach **Mike Shanahan** to go for a two-point conversion instead of a game-tying field goal at the end of a 27-26 loss to the [Atlanta Falcons](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/atl/atlanta-falcons) is as baffling as his decision to shut down a healthy **[Robert Griffin III](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/14875/robert-griffin)**. If you are showcasing **[Kirk Cousins](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/14880/kirk-cousins)** over three games, let the game go into overtime. Cousins completed 29 of 45 passes for 381 yards and looked like a quarterback who could net a first-round pick for the Redskins in a trade. The 320 offensive yards he posted in the first half were the most for a Redskins team since 1991. With 22 seconds left in regulation and trailing by one, Shanahan called for a Cousins pass that didn't connect with **[Pierre Garcon](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/11439/pierre-garcon)**. As a result, the Redskins are 3-11 and close to securing the No. 2 draft choice for the [St. Louis Rams](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/stl/st-louis-rams). If you are wondering, NFL teams have been successful on two-point conversions about 50 percent of the time this season.. ... How bad were things for [New York Giants](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/nyg/new-york-giants) quarterback **[Eli Manning](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/5526/eli-manning)** in a 23-0 loss to Seattle? Wide receiver **[Hakeem Nicks](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/12586/hakeem-nicks)** was asked about Manning's interceptions. "Which ones?" Nicks said. Manning threw five, including two each to **[Byron Maxwell](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/14133/byron-maxwell)** and **[Richard Sherman](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/14086/richard-sherman)**. Manning has 25 for the season. ... **[Russell Wilson](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/14881/russell-wilson)** led the Seahawks with 50 rushing yards. "We've never had a philosophy of featuring the QB," Seahawks coach **Pete Carroll** said. "We want him to be the one who distributes the ball in a balanced attack." Wilson might be changing that thinking. He's that good. ... It's starting to look as though **[Matt Cassel](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/8644/matt-cassel)** is the best quarterback to emerge in Minnesota this year. Cassel completed his first nine attempts in blowing out the Eagles and he has had the five longest completions of the season for the Vikings. Cassel threw for 382 yards and two touchdowns Sunday. ... Down five starters to injury, the [Indianapolis Colts](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/ind/indianapolis-colts) welcomed the return of AFC South play to fix what has ailed them for the past month. They blew out the [Houston Texans](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/hou/houston-texans), 25-3. They visit the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/kc/kansas-city-chiefs) next Sunday in what will be a playoff preview. If they lose, though, they will be 4-6 against the rest of the league and 5-0 against the AFC South. ... One thing stood out in the [Buffalo Bills](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/buf/buffalo-bills)' 27-20 win over Jacksonville. Their five sacks increased their season total to 49 and they became the second team since 1982 to have four players with at least eight sacks. The 2006 [Baltimore Ravens](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/bal/baltimore-ravens) were the only other team to have four players with that many. ... The NFC swept four games against the AFC on Sunday and won the interconference battle. The NFC has a 34-27 edge with only one game remaining. ... One of the motivations for the Panthers on Sunday was what Jets wide receiver **[Santonio Holmes](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/9611/santonio-holmes)** said about their secondary. He said it was the weak link of the Panthers' defense. In the 30-20 win over the Jets, the Panthers allowed only 140 net passing yards. ... The [Arizona Cardinals](https://www.espn.ph/nfl/team/_/name/ari/arizona-cardinals) kept their slight playoff hopes alive by beating the Titans in overtime, 37-34. Their challenge now is trying to beat Seattle and San Francisco in the final two games, which will be tough. Nevertheless, **Bruce Arians** and **[Carson Palmer](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4459/carson-palmer)** have done a great job getting Arizona to nine wins.

Published: Dec 15, 2013 at 12:27 PM

The [Jason Garrett](https://www.nfl.com/player/jasongarrett/2514652/profile) era in Dallas has been defined by excruciating, inexplicable losses. At times it feels like the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) are constructing games carefully in order to inflict the most pain on their fans and themselves.

It's going to be tough to top Sunday's loss.

1.  The [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) scored touchdowns on all five of their second-half possessions before kneeling the ball at the end of the game. A reminder: [Matt Flynn](https://www.nfl.com/player/mattflynn/367/profile) remains their quarterback.

2.  The [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) set a franchise record with 332 yards in the first half, jumped out to a 26-3 advantage -- and they still lost.

3.  Dallas took a 12-point lead with just over eight minutes left after [one of the greatest touchdown catches](http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-cant-miss-plays/0ap2000000298671/WK-15-Can-t-Miss-Play-Final-Dez-tination) you will ever see by wide receiver [Dez Bryant](https://www.nfl.com/player/dezbryant/497278/profile). And they still managed to lose.

4.  [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) quarterback [Tony Romo](https://www.nfl.com/player/tonyromo/2505354/profile) was intercepted on Dallas' final two drives. He made a terrible throw on a pass to [Miles Austin](https://www.nfl.com/player/milesaustin/2495801/profile) that set up the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) to take the lead. (Give [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) cornerback [Sam Shields](https://www.nfl.com/player/samshields/1037374/profile) a ton of credit for [making a terrific play](http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-game-highlights/0ap2000000298715/Romo-s-pass-intercepted-by-Shields), but it was a brutal throw and decision by Romo.) On Romo's [next interception](http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-game-highlights/0ap2000000298755/Tony-Romo-throws-game-ending-interception), there was a miscommunication with slot receiver [Cole Beasley](https://www.nfl.com/player/colebeasley/2535698/profile).

5.  Everyone will kill [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) coach [Jason Garrett](https://www.nfl.com/player/jasongarrett/2514652/profile) for throwing the ball so much late in the game. But Romo had two chances to end the game and he missed throws. If he completes a deep pass to an open [Dez Bryant](https://www.nfl.com/player/dezbryant/497278/profile) on the second-to-last drive, the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) win the game. He underthrew Bryant.

On Romo's first interception, [Miles Austin](https://www.nfl.com/player/milesaustin/2495801/profile) was open for a huge gain. Romo was pressured and made a bad throw. This was more about execution than coaching.

6.  Romo had a run-pass option on the throw to Austin.

"I think he'll be the first one to tell you he probably should have run the ball in that situation," coach [Jason Garrett](https://www.nfl.com/player/jasongarrett/2514652/profile) said after the game.

7.  This _feels_ like the end for the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL), but it's not at all. All they have to do is beat Washington next week to set up a potential win-and-in situation against Philadelphia in [Week 17](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013122903/2013/REG17/eagles@cowboys). The [Eagles](https://www.nfl.com/teams/philadelphiaeagles/profile?team=PHI)' loss in Minnesota on [Sunday](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013121505/2013/REG15/eagles@vikings) saved Dallas from early elimination.

Green Bay, meanwhile, is very much alive in the [NFC North race](http://www.nfl.com/playoffs/playoff-picture) at 7-6-1. If quarterback [Aaron Rodgers](https://www.nfl.com/player/aaronrodgers/2506363/profile) could somehow return next week, the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) could wind up winning their last two games and getting into the playoffs.

After seeing Flynn direct five consecutive touchdown drives, anything is possible.

The Sports Xchange

By Art Garcia, The Sports Xchange

Packers-Cowboys: What we learned

ARLINGTON, Texas — All but left for dead by the Dallas Cowboys, the Packers roared back for a 37-36 victory that keeps Green Bay very much alive in the NFC playoff race.

Quarterback Matt Flynn led an improbable second-half comeback as the Packers trailed 26-3 before scoring five touchdowns against a beleaguered Dallas defense, including running back Eddie Lacy’s game-winning 1-yarder with 1:31 remaining. Flynn threw four touchdowns after halftime.

“What a feeling,” Flynn said after his second straight win as starter. “We were all just sitting around at the end taking knees (and) we were like, ‘Is this real? Is this happening?'”

Green Bay (7-6-1) remained squarely in the playoff hunt with two games left. The Packers trail both Chicago (8-6) and Detroit (7-6) in the NFC North. Green Bay has games left with Pittsburgh and at Chicago.

The Packers could also get quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who missed his sixth straight game against Dallas, back in the lineup from the collarbone injury he suffered Nov. 4. Green Bay coach Mike McCarthy wasn’t tipping his hand about the status of his star quarterback.

“Nothing’s really changed,” McCarthy said.

The Cowboys (7-7) didn’t do themselves any favors with their second straight loss to a backup quarterback. Dallas does control its own destiny in the NFC East, despite being a game back of 8-6 Philadelphia.

The Cowboys end the season at home against the Eagles on Dec. 29 with the division title likely on the line. Dallas is at Washington next week.

“We are in the same situation we were in when we woke up this morning,” Dallas coach Jason Garrett said, referring to Philadelphia’s loss. “We have to put this one behind us.”

Dallas quarterback Tony Romo delivered the kind of December performance that has plagued him for much of his career. Romo, now 11-17 lifetime in the season’s final month, threw for 358 yards and two touchdowns, but had two costly interceptions in the fourth quarter. His second pick by cornerback Tramon Williams ended the game with 1:08 left in the game.

The Cowboys abandoned the running game in the second half despite a 23-point lead and DeMarco Murray piling up 93 yards at the break. The Cowboys averaged a staggering 7.4 yards per carry but with the ball and a lead late in the fourth quarter, Dallas continually put the ball in the air.

Garrett intimated that Romo audibled out of a number of runs in the second half.

“We decided to be a little more aggressive and felt it was the right approach with the way the game going,” Romo countered. “It’s easy to look back now and say run the ball, run the ball, run the ball.”

Flynn, the third consecutive backup quarterback to start against Dallas, threw for 299 yards, as the Packers spent most of the game playing catch-up.

Flynn’s 11-yard screen pass to James Starks early in the fourth pulled Green Bay within 29-24 before what nearly was another epic Romo mistake.

Williams appeared to intercept a tipped Romo pass on ensuing drive, returning the pick inside the Dallas 10. But the play was challenged and officials ruled the ball hit the ground as Williams was attempting to secure it.

With new life, Romo took the Cowboys the length of the field for a touchdown and 36-24 advantage. Receiver Dez Bryant hauled in a throw over Green Bay defenders in the back of the end zone.

Flynn again took the Packers down the field for a touchdown, connecting with receiver James Jones from three yards out with 4:23 left. Green Bay would get the ball back with 2:50 remaining.

This time Romo wasn’t as lucky, as cornerback Sam Shields picked up an intended throw for receiver Miles Austin at the 50-yard line. Lacy bowled in from the 1 seven plays later.

“It was a run call that he threw the ball on,” Garrett said.

Williams’ interception on Dallas’ last drive preserved the win. The play was initially rule a no-catch before replays reversed it to Williams’ and Green Bay’s satisfaction.

“The one that I didn’t get credited with, I thought I caught it,” Williams said. “But the one I did get credited with, I never felt more sure about a catch in my life.”

Lacy rushed for 141 yards, his fourth game at least 100, and upped his total to 1,028 on the season.

What the Packers said

“I was drained. Just to see the emotion of the guys, what the guys overcame. It took me everything not to cry.” — Coach Mike McCarthy, on the scene in the Green Bay locker room after the come-from-behind win.

What the Cowboys said

“Disappointing loss, no question about that, independent of what anybody else does.” — Coach Jason Garrett, on losing to the Green Bay Packers and missing an opportunity to overtake the Philadelphia Eagles in the NFC East.

What we learned about the Packers

1\. Matt Flynn is an effective Plan B at quarterback. The Packers remain without Aaron Rodgers, but Flynn proved capable enough Sunday. He threw four touchdown passes in the second half as Green Bay rallied to top the Dallas Cowboys.

“Matt just stays the course,” coach Mike McCarthy said.

2\. Green Bay is alive and well in the playoff hunt. The Packers are 7-6-1 with two games left: home against the Pittsburgh Steelers, then at the NFC North-leading Chicago Bears. Sweep the last two games, and Green Bay has a good shot.

What we learned about the Cowboys

1\. Dallas gets away from what is working at the most inopportune times. Running back DeMarco Murray ran for 93 yards on 11 carries in the first half, but he got only seven more attempts despite the team holding a 23-point halftime lead.

“At different times in the second half, we probably could have run the ball more,” coach Jason Garrett said.

2\. The defense isn’t likely to get any better. The Cowboys’ banged-up D gave up five touchdowns in the second half, continuing its season-long trend of ineptitude.

“We couldn’t get stops when we needed them,” Garrett said.

Updated July 10, 2025, 10:06 p.m. CT

The [Green Bay Packers](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/green-bay-packers/335) just finished up an incredible first 25 years of football in the 2000s. Between 2000 and 2024, the Packers won 251 regular season games (third most) and 15 playoff games (fifth most), including Super Bowl XLV.

The last 25 years included the final stretch of Brett Favre's Packers career, the legendary career of Aaron Rodgers and the start of the Jordan Love era.

To help celebrate, here are some of the best moments of the last 25 years in Packers football:

Packers win Super Bowl XLV
--------------------------

The 2010 Packers beat the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/pittsburgh-steelers/356) at AT&T Stadium in Dallas to win a fourth Lombardi Trophy and 13th world title.

[Super Bowl XLV: Steelers vs. Packers highlights](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=trjbUkBqM6o)

Rodgers to Cook stuns top-seeded Cowboys
----------------------------------------

Aaron Rodgers rolled left and hit Jared Cook for one of the most iconic completions in Packers history, helping set up a game-winning field goal as Green Bay took down the top-seeded Cowboys in the 2017 NFC Divisional Round.

[Aaron Rodgers' Clutch Pass to Jared Cook Sets Up Game-Winning FG! | NFL Divisional Highlights](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sVAECoucqNo)

Janis strikes twice
-------------------

In the 2015 NFC Divisional Round, Aaron Rodgers and Jeff Janis connected twice in the final minute to tie the [Cardinals](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/arizona-cardinals/355). Janis caught a 60-yard pass on 4th-and-20 and a 41-yard Hail Mary touchdown on the final play of regulation.

[HAIL MARY! Rodgers Prayers Answered Again! | Packers vs. Cardinals | NFL](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LwiBW6j80kI)

Cobb beats [Bears](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/chicago-bears/326), wins NFC North
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

On 4th-and-8, Aaron Rodgers found Randall Cobb all alone for a 48-yard touchdown that beat the Bears at Soldier Field and improbably won the Packers the NFC North title in 2013.

[Aaron Rodgers to Randall Cobb, 48-Yard TD Stuns the Bears (Week 17, 2013) | Packers vs. Bears | NFL - YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YXq8C5sbRzU)

Miracle in Motown
-----------------

"Does he have a vintage moment in him?" A 61-yard Hail Mary touchdown from Aaron Rodgers to Richard Rodgers stunned the [Lions](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/detroit-lions/334) at Ford Field.

[Aaron Rodgers' Amazing Hail Mary: The Miracle in Motown! | Packers vs. Lions | NFL](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r0vVqStvh_8)

BJ Raji pick-six in NFC title game
----------------------------------

B.J. Raji's pick-six of Caleb Hanie in the 2010 NFC Championship Game helped send the Packers to Super Bowl XLV.

[B.J. Raji's Awesome Pick Six & Dance vs. Bears (2010 NFC Championship Game) | NFL - YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Uqm9Gnd_FM)

Brett Favre overcomes passing of father, enjoys game of his life in Oakland
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

The day after his father passed, Brett Favre put on a show in a 41-7 win over the Oakland Raiders on "Monday Night Football" in 2003.

["Favre's Dad Game" | Brett Gives it All for Big Irv | A Football Life | NFL Films](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TsWq3cnp1qQ)

"He did what?!?"
----------------

Antonio Freeman's ridiculous catch in overtime beats the Vikings at Lambeau Field during the 2000 season and creates an iconic Al Michaels soundbite.

[Top 50 Sound FX | #18: Antonio Freeman's Improbable Bobble MNF OT Catch ("He did WHAT?!") | NFL](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lme6dBIGcfU)

Al Harris pulls out the dagger vs. Matt Hasselbeck
--------------------------------------------------

"We want the ball, and we're going to score." Famous last words from Matt Hasselbeck, who threw a pick-six to Packers cornerback Al Harris on the opening possession of overtime in the 2003 NFC Wild Card Round.

[Al Harris' Game-Winning Pick Six in OT | Seahawks vs Packers | 2003 NFC Wild Card Game Highlights - YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_RFOwmNDfPY)

Tramon Williams pick-six in Atlanta
-----------------------------------

The upset of the top-seeded Atlanta Falcons became very real when Tramon Williams intercepted Matt Ryan and returned the pick for a touchdown to end the first half of the 2010 NFC Divisional Round.

[Tramon Williams 70 Yard Pick 6 2010 NFC Divisional vs Falcons (4K60fps)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=57hkbOaowrI)

Rodgers takes out first-half flamethrower against Bears
-------------------------------------------------------

Six touchdown passes from Aaron Rodgers in the first half of a primetime game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. The first half score? 42-0 Packers.

[Aaron Rodgers 6 Touchdowns in One Half! (Bears vs. Packers, 2014) | NFL Vault Highlights](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4gWoSMk3tx4)

Rodgers to Cobb beats Bears again
---------------------------------

After returning from a knee injury and facing a 20-0 deficit, Aaron Rodgers threw a 75-yard touchdown pass late in the fourth quarter to complete the epic Week 1 comeback against the Bears to open 2018.

[Rodgers & Cobb's 75-Yd TD Connection to Take the Lead!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I40ILjNdwZM)

The Cobb Hail Mary
------------------

The master of the Hail Mary struck again, finding Randall Cobb to end the first half of a playoff win over the New York Giants at Lambeau Field in the 2016 NFC Wild Card Round.

[Aaron Rodgers Hail Mary Before Half! | Giants vs. Packers | NFL Wild Card Highlights](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NiaBRtImvYU)

Favre and Jennings walk off in Denver
-------------------------------------

On the first play of overtime, Brett Favre hit Greg Jennings for a walk-off 82-yard touchdown pass to beat the Denver Broncos during the 2007 season.

[2007 Favre Connects with Jennings for 82-Yard TD in OT | NFL](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZynxowoYrs4)

Run The Table
-------------

"I feel like we can run the table, I really do." Aaron Rodgers sends a message, and then walks the walk during a legendary run to end the 2016 season.

[Run The Table - The Movie](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6TxbBHVHYk)

I still own you!
----------------

"I still own you!" Aaron Rodgers asserts his ownership over the Bears after a touchdown run at Soldier Field in 2021.

["I Still Own You" -Aaron Rodgers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u1dFr4V_RIA)

Rodgers threads the needle to Rodgers
-------------------------------------

Aaron Rodgers hit Richard Rodgers in a tiny window while rolling to his left for a touchdown, giving the Packers a fourth quarter lead in a win over the Cowboys in the 2014 NFC Divisional Round.

[Cowboys vs. Packers 2014 Divisional Round highlights](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=keU-IqHJDL4)

Packers vs. Patriots at Lambeau in 2014
---------------------------------------

One of the best regular season games of the last 25 years of Packers football.

[Brady & Rodgers Meeting While Both Teams Peak! (Patriots vs. Packers 2014, Week 13)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3V3cxUvnw_o)

Matt Flynn engineers epic comeback against Cowboys
--------------------------------------------------

The Packers trailed the Cowboys 26-3 at halftime in 2013. Then Matt Flynn happened. The Packers won 37-36 to keep their season alive.

[Mighty Matt Flynn’s Epic Comeback! (Packers vs. Cowboys 2013, Week 15)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Ym77sBEBks)

Packers become first No. 7 seed to win playoff game in blowout against Cowboys
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Packers jumped out to a 27-0 lead and cruised to a 48-32 win over the second-seeded Cowboys at AT&T Stadium in the 2023 NFC Wild Card Round.

[Green Bay Packers vs. Dallas Cowboys Game Highlights | NFL 2023 Super Wild Card Weekend](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRhRhGIWqQA)

Randall Cobb sets kickoff return record in first NFL game
---------------------------------------------------------

Randall Cobb, a rookie in 2011, returned a kickoff 108 yards for a touchdown in his NFL debut against the New Orleans Saints at Lambeau Field.

[Randall Cobb 108 yard Kick Return](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cYfm-2f_XBw)

Honorable mentions
------------------

*   Packers clinch playoff spot with wild Vikings defeat in season finale (2003)
*   Brett Favre sets NFL passing touchdown record against Vikings (2007)
*   Rodgers returns from calf injury, takes down Lions to clinch NFC North (2014)
*   Donald Driver rumbles to long touchdown vs. 49ers (2010)
*   Brett Favre underhands touchdown pass in snowy playoff game vs. [Seahawks](https://sportsdata.usatoday.com/football/nfl/teams/seattle-seahawks/361) (2007)
*   Aaron Rodgers to Davante Adams beats Cowboys late (2017)
*   Packers kick late FG, win NFC North at Metrodome (2004)
*   Ahman Green scores 98-yard rushing touchdown (2003)
*   Tramon Williams intercepts Michael Vick to secure playoff win over Eagles (2010)
*   Aaron Rodgers fake spike, go-ahead TD vs. Dolphins (2014)
*   Jordan Love leads comeback from 17-0 down in first start at Lambeau (2023)
*   Aaron Rodgers hits Greg Jennings for TD to complete comeback over Bears (2009)
*   Matt Flynn throws six touchdown passes in season finale win over Lions (2011)
*   Rasul Douglas intercepts Kyler Murray after signing off Cardinals practice squad (2021)

PUBLISHED: December 15, 2013 at 7:42 PM CST | UPDATED: November 8, 2015 at 8:35 AM CST

**Getting your [Trinity Audio](https://trinityaudio.ai/) player ready...**

ARLINGTON, Texas—Tony Romo had no interest in ranking just how bad this loss was for the Dallas Cowboys after throwing two interceptions in the final 3 minutes.

Owner Jerry Jones was a bit more forthright after the 37-36 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, when the Cowboys blew a 23-point lead in the second half in a defeat that kept them from getting back in the NFC East lead with two games to play.

“This is one of the hardest losses that I’ve experienced. That’s a shame that we’ve lost that ballgame,” Jones said. “When you have that kind of lead and you are playing well, and we were playing well, then it’s a shame to lose a ballgame like that.”

With their second loss in the row, after Philadelphia lost earlier in the day, the Cowboys (7-7) remained a game behind the Eagles.

A week after Chicago scored on eight consecutive possessions against them, the Cowboys watched Green Bay get touchdowns on their first five drives after halftime. The Packers’ last possession was Matt Flynn kneel-downs after Tramon Williams’ diving pick that was initially called an incompletion before being overturned on a video review.

“We’ve got two weeks to get this thing right,” cornerback Brandon Carr said. “Right now, words really have no effect. Complete debacle in the second half.”

This is arguably the worst loss in the Jones era, even though it wasn’t their biggest blown lead. The Cowboys led by 24 points in the third quarter at home two years ago against Detroit, which rallied for a 34-30 victory in a game when Romo had two interceptions returned for touchdowns.

“We’ve had some big wins, a couple of tough losses this year. This obviously falls into that tough loss category,” Romo said. “We still control what we feel like we can get done. It just doesn’t feel like it right now because we let slip away.”

Yes, Dallas can still be the NFC East champion by winning next week at Washington and then in the Dec. 29 home finale against the Eagles. The Cowboys are 4-0 vs. NFC East teams so far this season.

“Real tough loss for us out there. This is unbelievable,” Jones said. “But as it turns out we win the next two ballgames then we are exactly in the same spot as we were at 3:30 this afternoon.”

Flynn, in very possibly his last start for Green Bay (7-6-1) before Aaron Rodgers returns, threw four touchdowns in the second half. Eddie Lacy had the winning score on a 1-yard plunge with 1:31 left after the first pick by Romo.

Playing on the same field where they won the 2011 Super Bowl, the Packers matched the biggest comeback in team history. Green Bay rallied past the Los Angeles Rams after trailing by 23 in the 1982 season opener.

Dez Bryant, who had 153 yards receiving, had picked up a first down just before the 2-minute warning. But Romo threw behind Miles Austin after escaping a sack and Sam Shields got an interception at midfield. The Packers steadily moved downfield before the plunge by Lacy, who had 141 yards rushing.

Bryant had a 5-yard TD midway through the fourth quarter for a 36-24 lead, on a drive that included another near interception by Williams that was overturned on a review after being called a pick.

Dallas took only two more snaps after Lacy’s go-ahead TD. Cole Beasley made a 9-yard catch before getting out of bounds, and Romo was throwing his way again when Williams made the game-clinching play.

“We played very well in the first half and gave ourselves a great opportunity to win this ballgame by how well we played early, and then we didn’t play well in the second half. It’s just as simple as that,” coach Jason Garrett said. “We didn’t get stops on defense. We didn’t sustain enough drives. We had to kick too many field goals.”

Bryant walked off the field before the game ended and refused to talk to reporters in the locker room. Instead, he simply shook his head at them.

Dan Bailey kicked five field goals, including two 50-yarders.

As for Garrett, who led the Cowboys to 8-8 records in each of his two full seasons without getting to the playoffs, Jones emphatically repeated that there will be no coaching change, no matter what happens.

“We have to rebound. We’ve got a ball game coming up, and by the way, Garrett will coach that game against the Redskins. Book that. Write about that,” Jones said. “He will coach the ballgame we have coming up and as far as I can see in the future he will be coaching the games for the Cowboys. It’s a setback for everybody. It’s not just on one guy.”

NOTES: Romo threw for 358 yards, breaking a four-game streak without topping 250. … DeMarco Murray had 134 yards rushing and a touchdown for the Cowboys.

Arlington, TX (SportsNetwork.com) - Eddie Lacy's 1-yard touchdown run with 1:31 to play completed an epic Green Bay comeback as the Packers got past the Dallas Cowboys, 37-36.

Trailing by 23 points to start the second half, Green Bay scored touchdowns on its first five possessions of the final 30 minutes, while Tony Romo had another meltdown in the fourth quarter.

With the victory, Green Bay (7-6-1) has managed to stay alive in the chase for the NFC North crown thanks to consecutive wins despite signal-caller Aaron Rodgers still on the sideline as he recovers from a fractured collarbone.

The Packers sit in third place in the NFC North, behind Chicago (8-6) and Detroit (7-6). Detroit hosts the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night.

Matt Flynn, Rodgers' replacement under center, threw for 299 yards and four touchdowns with an interception on 26-of-39 passing, with Lacy finishing the game with 141 yards on 21 carries and a score while adding four catches for 30 yards.

Dallas (7-7), meanwhile, stays a game back of Philadelphia for first place in the NFC East, as the Eagles lost to the Vikings on Sunday.

Romo looked strong for much of the game and went 29-for-48 for 358 yards and two touchdowns overall, but his final two possessions ended in interceptions. The first one led to Lacy's go-ahead score and his second sealed the victory for Green Bay.

DeMarco Murray had another strong game for Dallas, carrying the ball 18 times for 134 yards and a score along with four catches for 19 yards.
